title: Effects of continuous moderate exercise with partial blood flow restriction during hemodialysis: A protocol for a randomized clinical trial
author: Cardoso, Araujo, et al.

steps.title: Obtain informed consent
steps.instruction: After recruitment, have each patient sign the informed consent form and record enrollment.

steps.title: Schedule baseline and follow‑up assessments
steps.instruction: Plan baseline and post‑intervention measurements for week 1 as follows: 1st HD session – resting heart rate, resting blood pressure, ankle‑arm index, and questionnaire; 2nd HD session – body‑fat percentage, body mass, height, and blood collection after dialysis; 3rd HD session – 6‑minute walk test and muscle‑strength dynamometry. Apply the same distribution for final evaluations.

steps.title: Measure vital signs and anthropometrics
steps.instruction: Measure blood pressure with an analog sphygmomanometer (accuracy 1.0 mm Hg) and stethoscope (BD, Brazil); record body mass and height with a digital scale (resolution 0.1 kg/0.1 cm, Filizola, Brazil) and calculate BMI; measure heart rate with a Polar digital monitor (Finland).

steps.title: Measure ankle‑arm index
steps.instruction: Have the patient rest supine ≥10 min; measure arm systolic pressure with an analog sphygmomanometer on the arm without the fistula; measure ankle systolic pressure with a 5–8 MHz vascular Doppler, cuff placed ~3 inches above the malleolus; calculate AAI = higher ankle pressure × higher arm pressure − 1.

steps.title: Ultrasound quadriceps thickness
steps.instruction: Using a MicroMaxx (Sonosite) ultrasound, mark two reference points on each quadriceps: (1) midpoint between the anterior superior iliac spine and the patella’s upper pole, and (2) border of the lower third and upper two‑thirds between the same landmarks; capture a frozen image and measure the distance from the femoral bone’s upper margin to the deep fascia of the rectus femoris, including rectus femoris and vastus medialis.

steps.title: Bioelectrical impedance for body fat
steps.instruction: Perform multifrequency BIA with a Quadscan4000 (Bodystat) while the subject lies supine, arms stretched along the trunk, legs apart; clean skin with alcohol and place electrodes ≥5 cm apart; conduct the assessment 20–30 min after the middle‑week HD session; calculate % body fat using the manufacturer’s equation.

steps.title: Pre‑measurement participant instructions
steps.instruction: Instruct patients to avoid any physical exercise for 8 h and to refrain from alcohol, chocolate, coffee, tea, and energy drinks for 12 h before the exam; schedule body‑composition and muscle‑thickness measurements 20–30 min after the HD session.

steps.title: Collect and process blood samples
steps.instruction: A trained nurse draws 10 mL of blood from the fistula, 5 mL into a clot‑activator tube and 5 mL into an anticoagulant tube; separate and store whole blood and isolate the erythrocyte fraction for oxidative‑stress assays; collect samples at baseline, after the third training session, at the end of weeks 6 and 12 (end of each mesocycle), and 48 h after the final exercise session.

steps.title: ELISA for cytokines and CRP
steps.instruction: Measure serum IL‑6, IL‑10, and CRP using DuoSet ELISA kits (R&D Systems, USA) following the manufacturer’s protocol; read absorbance at 450 nm; run all samples and standards in duplicate with a coefficient of variation < 5%; express results in pg/mL.

steps.title: Measure oxidative‑stress enzymes
steps.instruction: Determine catalase, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione peroxidase activities with the RANSEL® kit (Randox Lab, UK) using the method of Misra and Fridovich.

steps.title: Conduct 6‑minute walk test
steps.instruction: On a 30‑m flat track marked every 3 m, have the patient sit for 10 min to stabilize vitals, then walk as far as possible for 6 min at maximal speed; perform the test before the HD session.

steps.title: Static knee‑extension strength test
steps.instruction: Using a Crown® dynamometer, instruct the patient to stand on the base with knees flexed ≈120°, spine upright, arms at sides, elbows extended; reset the device, then have the patient produce maximal knee‑extension force while avoiding spine, arm, or backward body movement; perform two trials with a 1‑min interval and record the mean value.

steps.title: Randomize and run exercise intervention
steps.instruction: After baseline collection, randomly assign participants to BFRG, EG, or CG; conduct a 12‑week program with three weekly sessions (≥1 day between sessions); ensure physical therapists and physical‑education teachers monitor exercise execution, BFR device use, and heart‑monitor compliance.

steps.title: Data entry and statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Enter all data twice in EPIDATA 3.1 to detect inconsistencies; set significance at 5 %; analyze data in Stata 14.0 using mixed‑factor ANOVA with Bonferroni post‑hoc for parametric variables and Kruskal‑Wallis with Dunn post‑hoc for non‑parametric variables; the analyst remains blinded to study objectives.
